_comment: Independent-implementability ledger (SPEC §13). One record per blind
implementation attempt. This file is an ASSERTION about runs that happened;
scripts/check-implementability.py machine-checks the half that can be checked
— that each surface_digest is exactly what blind-export.py reproduces from the
recorded source — and enforces the structural rules §13 states. The verdict
itself is attested by the implementer and cannot be re-derived by CI, which is
why it carries the evidence pointer rather than standing alone.
Rounds are append-only. A superseded verdict is never edited: it is a fact
about a surface that existed, and later repair does not make it untrue.

rounds.surface_note: NOT RECORDED. This run predates blind-export.py and ran in a git worktree, so the supplied surface was not pinned by a manifest and cannot be reconstructed exactly. Per §13.3 the claim is therefore unbound, and is retained as history rather than as evidence.
inferred: the entire model lattice, reverse-engineered from vectors; the Apache-2.0 row was demonstrably free — all-UNSTATED, all-YES and all-NO each still passed 8/8
§12.4 encoding details not stated in that section
contamination: two commit SUBJECT LINES reached the agent's terminal via `git checkout` and `git log --oneline -1`; isolation was instructional rather than structural
part of §12 was repaired in 234e3ee between dispatch and return, so the run partly tested a document that no longer existed
rounds.implementer_statement: A reader with §12 and no fixtures cannot produce a single verdict. The vectors are functioning as normative text here.

It reports they contain no mention of licences, evaluation, grants, the lattice, or anything in §12 — recorded as a fact rather than weighed as a judgement

the subject read scripts/license-rule-matrix.py before the vector boundary (it is a named input) and discloses that its EXPECTED label for LICENSE-POLICY-DEFINED influenced one pre-boundary assumption
rounds.implementer_statement: A working implementation exists and reproduces 23 of 25 vectors on its first run. But several encoding details were not determined by the prose, and two fixtures are not reproducible from the specification at all.
rounds.constructive_note: On failing to reproduce two published fixtures the implementer searched over 160,000 candidate encodings, declined to infer the missing sentinel, and reported the fixtures as irreproducible rather than adjusting until they matched. 23/25 carrying that refusal is stronger evidence than 25/25 obtained by adaptation: it is the first round demonstrating resistance to teaching-to-the-test, and it is what exposed an undocumented constant in the reference.

rounds.hypothesis: The declared normative surface — this document plus the normative data §13.1b incorporates — is now sufficient for an independent implementation of §12 WITHOUT INFERENCE. Recorded BEFORE dispatch so it is falsifiable rather than narrated afterwards: if the round returns PASS-WITH-INFERENCE, this hypothesis is disproved and the inferred list says exactly where the surface is still incomplete.
rounds.prediction: If a defect is found it will most likely NOT be in licensing. §13.1a/§13.1b created a new abstraction — the prose/normative-data boundary — and this run is its first independent user, so the likeliest findings are that a declared schema constrains one thing and not another, that an artifact's interpretation is still implied rather than stated, or that the versioning rule is underspecified.
rounds.constructive_note: Three vectors turn on one undetermined clause — what to EMIT for an unrecognised policy. The implementer identified that both readings satisfy the stated rule, declined to adopt the fixtures' reading because doing so would be inference, and left the vectors failing. It also ran the alternative reading in a separate probe, confirmed all three reproduce exactly under it, and did not modify the implementation.
rounds.prediction_outcome: PARTLY CONFIRMED. The prediction was that findings would fall at the prose/normative-data boundary. The implementer called that boundary 'the best-specified part of §12' — so the prediction was wrong about where the WEAKNESS was — but it still yielded three real defects there: model retrieval unspecified, consumer behaviour on a malformed model undefined, and no obligation to RECOMPUTE model-digest. The largest findings were elsewhere: the identity never bound its subject.
inferred: what to EMIT for an unrecognised policy — the rule named a prohibition and never defined the behaviour; cost three vectors

contamination: the subject disclosed prior familiarity: its session context carried the project's CLAUDE.md and a memory index, unsought and undeclinable. It reports the §12 material there is nil and licence evaluation is unmentioned, and assesses that it gave no rule but may have made §8.2.2/§9 cross-references quicker to place
it ran `wc -l` on the vector file during manifest verification before the boundary, so it knew the record COUNT (30) while writing its predictions; disclosed there at the time, no content seen
after the first run it probed an alternative policy reading against three fixtures; labelled post-hoc, and the implementation was not changed
rounds.implementer_statement: A working implementation came out of the prose plus model.json, but eleven things were not determined by them, and I left three vectors failing rather than tune to them.
